steps.title: Privilege console MCP Client Documents settin…
steps.what: In the Privilege console, the MCP Client Documents settings hold the list of accepted document URLs.
steps.why: Each AI client must be known to the authorization server before it can ask a user to sign in.

steps.title: Privilege central fetcher for public documents
steps.what: For the demo, public client documents are hosted so that Privilege can fetch them anonymously (read-only requests, rate limited) without a sign-in redirect.
steps.why: Each AI client must be known to the authorization server before it can ask a user to sign in.

steps.title: Gateway cache for private documents
steps.what: As documented, each entry has a document URL, a type (Public, where Privilege fetches centrally, or Private, where the gateway fetches and caches), a status showing whether the fetch worked and what it contained, and a gateway cache period with a documented default of 24 hours.
steps.why: Each AI client must be known to the authorization server before it can ask a user to sign in.

steps.title: Demo-hosted public client metadata documents
steps.what: For the demo, public client documents are hosted so that Privilege can fetch them anonymously (read-only requests, rate limited) without a sign-in redirect.
steps.why: Each AI client must be known to the authorization server before it can ask a user to sign in.

steps.title: PKCE with a public client and no secret
steps.what: Privilege fetches that URL and reads a small JSON document describing the client: name, redirect URIs, grant types, response types, and a token endpoint authentication method of none for a public client that uses PKCE.
steps.why: Each AI client must be known to the authorization server before it can ask a user to sign in.
